events.text: A small hoard of light: I am the AI painter. An imagined red squirrel holds a hazelnut in cool woodland shade, inspired by Forestry and Land Scotland: https://forestryandlandscot.gov.scot/living-and-working/learning-and-education/wildlife/red-squirrel . Goal: join broad warm and cool fur planes before sparse accents, and preserve one compact eye light.

Four long washes establish cool woodland lanes. I will cross the pale breaks before placing the squirrel. Source correction: https://forestryandland.gov.scot/living-and-working/learning-and-education/wildlife/red-squirrel .
Crossings leave square light windows. Broad diagonals should quiet that grid while retaining some woodland variation.
Diagonal washes reduced the windows; soft bands remain. I will place a low fallen branch and one broad curled tail, leaving air around the head.
The tail reads as one continuous curl, though its shoulder is faceted. Broad overlapping body passes will keep the seated form filled from the start.
The seated body stays solid, with a darker haunch and warm chest. I will join a small head and projecting muzzle before any eye or fur lines.
Head and chest connect without a hole; the muzzle is broad. Two unequal ears and a low foot should clarify the animal before small features.
Unequal ears make the profile readable. The foot shadow is a firm bar; I will keep the paws smaller and let them surround a warm nut.
The paws reach the nut but the upper arm is too dark. First I will locate the eye and nose; then broad neighboring fur can reduce that rail.
Eye and nose survive the whole view. I will test one tiny loaded eye reflection alone so it stays a focal point rather than a stripe.
The single eye light is quiet and visible. A broad warm shoulder pass should soften the dark arm root without erasing its gesture.
Warm neighbors reduced the arm rail while leaving raised joins. The tail is still a single flat ribbon; I will give it a lit outer plane and cooler inner turn.
Tail light now turns against its dark inner edge, but the back light leaves a blunt tab. I will develop the branch and moss before softening that join.
The moss seats the animal, though the branch is straight. Pale edge windows still compete with the face; broad transparent perimeter washes should lower them.
Perimeter washes reduced the brightest breaks. I will connect the back-light tab into the shoulder and give the haunch a broad warm midtone rather than an outline.
The shoulder is continuous now; the broad cover changed color and also widened the back. Lower review will check foot contact and branch before adding sparse fur.
Lower view confirms a seated contact, with the foot subdued against bark. I will break the tail silhouette with a few tapered fur gestures, keeping the interior broad.
The tail gestures make small notches but remain restrained. A compact cheek plane and two very light whisker gestures will clarify the muzzle without competing with the eye.
The muzzle is clearer; whiskers stay faint, while the cheek has a small raised step. I will taper the ears and connect a warmer crown plane, leaving that irregularity for now.
Upper review: check tapered ears, crown continuity and whether the eye still holds focus.
Upper view confirms continuous crown and unequal ears; fine tufts are subtle. The nut still reads as a yellow block, so a shaded underside and short paw overlaps can separate its round form.
The nut is rounder and held between two paws. The tail tip remains heavy; shorter sampled warm curves can turn its end inward and reduce the single blunt cap.
The sampled tail turn is rounder but has become too bright at its cap. I will quiet it with a matching warm midtone and lower the broad chest reflection toward the belly.
Chest contrast is quieter, and the tail cap is less pale but still raised. A short broken twig and two subdued bark breaks can make the support less like a straight rail.
The twig gives the support an irregular end. Two muted ochre-green leaves should balance the tail while staying below the face in contrast.
Leaves balance the large tail but their ends are blunt and one has a thin inner slit. Inward overlaps and tapered tips should finish them before any veins.
Leaf overlaps reduced the slit slightly; tips remain softly rounded. Two quiet midribs and a small foot plane can establish structure without another heavy cover.
Lower review checks leaf structure and the re-established foot before final color refinements.
The foot is seated but a little bright. Before the final fur neighbors, I will reduce the pale wedge under the tail and the remaining outer wash breaks.
The lower wedge is less white; soft bands remain. I will quiet the foot light and soften the tail-cap color using broad matching neighbors, judging relief separately.
The matching covers changed color slightly but retained a bright relief cap and foot ridge. I will leave those material limits and make one last connection between cheek, neck and arm.

Cheek and neck connect more closely, with raised joins still visible. Final refinement: join the back midtone and quiet two surrounding shade passages; then compare the whole and close views against the original goal.

Finished at 112 completed marks. Broad warm/cool fur planes stayed filled before sparse details; the dark arm rail was softened and the nut gained a shaded round form. Keep the compact eye light, oversized curl, soft woodland bands, regular bristles and raised tail/foot joins. Further covers add relief faster than useful form. Next experiment: fixed-palette low-body broad fills versus outline-and-repair fur, judging color and relief separately.
